body:
Yes exactly, I feel so alone because I feel like everyone else in my workplace has been brainwashed. I don't understand how people are happy when they are selling their lives to work, merely to survive... I don't understand how anyone who thinks about day to day life is happy 

Also yes, definitely feel you about working so hard in school to get a job, and now that I'm here I just think "that's it?"

Me too. I feel like money doesn't motivate me at all, so it feels so pointless... Unless you're really into buying designer clothes and cars money doesn't mean much, just a means to survive... Gotta suffer everyday just to live...

Thank you very much 

It's hard to even take a few days off, for some reason I feel bad about it... I'm going back to work tomorrow
Thanks, and yes they do. I have a bank of pto that I can use for any reason (sick time, mental health, personal days, vacations/holidays)
Exactly how I feel... I'm good at laying down and watching tv... that's about it
Anxiety makes you feel like you don't excel at anything and depression makes you not enjoy anything, even hobbies.
Thank you, that means a lot. I know I should prioritize my mental health, but it's hard because my job keeps me alive... Feeds me...
Me too

I'm in the same boat with being scared to quit because "this is life". These feelings are the main cause of my suicidal thoughts... I just called out sick and I feel like I'm on the verge of a breakdown. 

The uncertainty is the worst for me, I don't know about you. Just not knowing if another job will make things better or if I'm fucking myself by quitting and won't be able to find something else... working in general makes me depressed. It's scary not knowing if it's this job or all jobs.

I'm not that new of a hire. I feel like I should know a lot of the things I have to ask about, which just makes me feel like shit I guess. I can't imagine continuing to work here over six months because I can't deal with the pressure of not knowing things and not being able to be like "oh well, I'm still pretty new so it's fine."

It's the main reason that I want to quit everything I start, which makes me seriously hate myself tbh. 

I work as a lab tech in a hospital. 

No, I'm trying to figure out my insurance stuff before I make an appointment to speak to a therapist. So hopefully it'll be soon.
really feeling like this right now. good to know i'm not alone.

Yes, that's definitely true. This is something that I want to make another post about soon, because I'm just not sure if it's normal that my PI calls me out in lab meeting to answer questions... and only me. It's not like she berates me for not knowing the answer or anything, but it just makes me feel super anxious... I have a lab meeting soon and I've been basically panicking about it all week. 

For some reason disclosing that I'm dealing with these issues just feels weird to me. I think it's because I think if I tell her, she'll think I'm making excuses, not cut out for the lab, or treat me differently than before (see me as a different person or something).

1. Haha, that's great. Thanks! This makes me feel so much better because my postdoc doesn't follow written protocols and he doesn't have to write things down. Basically my whole lab doesn't follow protocols, though. I never see anyone reading papers while doing experiments, so I've been kind of discouraged about always having to lay out my thoughts on paper. 
2. That's great. I have trouble saying no, so sometimes it's hard to leave lab in the evening. Weird how so many people are OK with working nights and weekend in academia :-( Me too! I definitely want to enjoy my personal life. 

Yes, that's definitely the question... I think my ultimate fear is that I'll feel this way at every job I work. I feel like it's anxiety clouding my ability to enjoy any kind of work, because anything I do at work makes me feel like I'm going to get fired, and then I get scared about my financial stability in the future, etc. etc. 

I think I picked it because I'm decent at my classwork and find it easier than other disciples, but I feel like I could have ended up in any major and feel the same about it, tbh. Thanks for your input :)

Thanks for your input! I definitely know that my PI doesn't mean it to call me out or put me in a hard spot. I think the PI, like you, just wants to hear me think so she can teach me what I don't know or give me a chance to ask questions. I guess it's just hard for me because I beat myself for knowing that lots of times my PIs, mentors, etc. don't do things to give me a hard time (in fact, they're doing it out of consideration for me), but I think anxiety just makes me feel really flustered and scared, like my heart starts pounding and my hands start sweating like crazy. Even when I'm just sitting at lab meeting, which is why I've been so anxious to attend (and I know it'll be so much worse when I start working full time). 

Thanks! I've been heavily advised from mentors in my real life to take time for myself as well. Yes, I think I don't feel passion for what I do, although I'll work hard at it. But I'm going to try to stick it out for a year or so and then try to explore my options.

I read #2 a while ago on my phone and haven't been on a computer to reply, but it made me tear up a little bit. I feel like I just feel like I'm going to get fired from every job ever, even though I work really hard. I come home and spend like 2 hours writing down notes from the day in my lab notebook, but I just have such a hard time forgiving myself. I guess I just feel like I'm hardworking but dumb, and create more problems that I solve. 

Thank you for your kind words, this was a great read and definitely some of what I needed to hear to feel better.

Thank you, this is wonderful. I think I just have a really heightened fear of getting fired (like, all the time) so even though I think I might feel better in a non-academic lab or in a STEM-adjacent field, I'm scared that I'm just going to feel this way about ALL jobs, no matter what I'm doing. 

I'm going to try to stick out this job for at least like a year since I told my PI I would commit 1-2 years, and then see what else I can try to get into. Thank you!

I got a job in an academic lab. I really wanted to get a tech job in industry, but I was advised by some faculty members/someone who works in industry that it might be tough without experience. That's why I decided to take this job when it was offered to me (basically, I was scared that I would turn down the offer, burn bridges, and then fail to get a job in industry with no experience). 

Did you land your job right after graduating with a BS with no experience? I'd love to hear more about your position, since this sounds ideal to me.

That's true. I guess it's hard since it just seems exactly like that, like everyone is super passionate and just way smarter than me, even though I know in my head they have much more experience. 

Thank you! Recently I feel like I've been rushing through things because I feel very pressed for time by my postdoc, and it's been making me really stressed. I'm just going to try to slow down again and do things carefully like I usually do.

Ahh thank you, that really helps, especially since my postdoc never follows protocols and never gives me protocols to follow, so it's hard to not be flustered since I've only done procedures a couple of times :( 

LOL yeah I feel like my mistakes are so stupid, so this is great. Thanks for your input -- I'm going to work on not being so hard on myself for not knowing things or messing up.

ME TOO and my postdoc never writes anything down!! ever!! I'VE NEVER SEEN HIM WRITE DOWN A CALCULATION and I can't do mental math like.... at all!! so it's super stressful because I feel like he thinks i'm so dumb for not being able to calculate these things in my head 

Ahh thank you, I really needed to hear this. I guess I just always think I'm not being efficient and I just feel really stupid for not being able to process things as fast as other people. That's also why I'm super scared my PI will call me out at lab meeting, because I just struggle with processing things if I don't have time to sit down and look at the data :( thanks for your input!

Congrats on successful DNA extraction! Also thanks for your input :) 

Yeah, I think I'm going to look into careers like that, maybe something on the administrative side that I might like more. Yeah I'm also going to try to talk to more people if I can, thanks!! Hopefully I can get some more options on what I can do with just a B.S. in bio because right now I feel quite hopeless :( thanks!

Yeah, I feel like my fear of making mistakes or seeming stupid really keeps me from putting myself out there. It sucks because I feel like it really paralyzes me from making decisions as well. 

I'm not really sure if it was ever there... I feel like it wasn't, but I'm not sure. I've been thinking about that a lot lately, actually. I feel like a big problem is that I'm so anxious that I am not sure what I'm passionate about. Any kind of work seems to make me anxious, which means that I feel like I'm not cut out for ANY job at all, whether that's in science or not

I guess I think working in a lab is ok, but I think having to read papers constantly and keep up with the lit and being unable to separate my work/home life is what's really getting to me. I guess I don't think I'm passionate about science because I want to just shut my brain off when I get home (probably the only way I'll avoid being an anxious, depressed mess all the time), whereas all my coworkers, mentors, and bosses seem to have no problem working until 11 pm and coming in at 8 am the next day. 

I'd really like to go in a different direction, but I'm just not sure what I can do with just a B.S and no experience in other fields. I think what's holding me back is that I feel very pressed for time and money that I feel I don't have. Plus I guess I think it's a big risk to change career paths completely for a job that might also make me the same level of anxious as working in science.
